title: Unit – 4 : Session – 9 : SLO – 1  |  Pipelining — Choose the Correct Answer
sections: 1. b) Increase instruction throughput — pipelining overlaps stages so more instructions complete per unit time.
2. b) 5 — the classic RISC pipeline has 5 stages: Fetch, Decode, Execute, Memory, Write-back.
3. b) Data hazard — an instruction needing the not-yet-written result of a previous instruction.
4. b) Branch prediction — guesses the branch outcome to keep the pipeline full through control hazards.
5. c) Fetch — the IF stage reads the instruction from memory.
6. c) Stall — a pipeline bubble is a stall cycle where no useful work advances.
7. a) Speedup = Non-pipelined time / Pipelined time.
9. b) Bypass unit — forwarding (bypassing) routes ALU results directly to where they are needed.
10. a) Longest pipeline stage — the slowest stage fixes the clock period and hence caps the speedup.
